clue.text: Hit first button — ultimately receive gift

parts.note: to press a button is to hit it
button one, written as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: last letter of receive

explanation.surface: Someone presses the first button on a machine and finally gets a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit first button' reads as one instruction: press button I, with I as the Roman numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressie is informal British slang for a present, which is a gift handed to someone.

clue.text: Large bird in lake, one tucking into nut

indicators.note: something in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A big bird bobs on a lake, one of them pecking at a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: Both lake and one go inside the nut, side by side, splitting it after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a very large waterbird famous for its throat pouch used for scooping fish.

clue.text: Guy looking up, dismissing a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the letters read from bottom to top
to dismiss is to send away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a guy is a male
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A man gazes upward, then waves away a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing MALE gives ELAM; dropping its A leaves ELM.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a common deciduous hardwood, once lining British fields and roadsides.

clue.text: Bound to have married during relationship in October down under?

parts.note: to bound is to spring, as in a leap

indicators.note: what happens during a period sits within it, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a tie is a bond or relationship
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to have married during an October relationship in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'obliged to'; it is a leap. Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere, so October falls in spring there.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia and other southern hemisphere countries, October is in the middle of the spring season.

clue.text: Praise upholding Christmas, omitting line about fireplace item?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is wrapped round another
in a down clue, holding something up turns it so it reads bottom to top
to omit is to leave out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Yule is an old name for Christmas
L for line, the letter removed
a log burns in a fireplace

explanation.surface: Praise for Christmas, minus a line, about the yule log by the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plants the familiar Christmas yule log, but its two halves are clued separately and used in different ways. Yule is an old word for the Christmas season.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly, often at a funeral.

clue.text: Get through article about sport? On the contrary

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another
this flips the stated relationship, so the outer and inner roles swap

parts.note: to sport clothes is to wear them
the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to read an article about sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the article goes around sport; 'On the contrary' reverses that, so sport (WEAR) goes around the article. 'Sport' is a verb here, not games.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather a storm or crisis is to come safely through it, to survive and endure it.

clue.text: Hang on — about to leave Holland in a French carriage?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the others

parts.note: to hang on is to wait
to go is to leave
NL is the international code for the Netherlands

explanation.surface: Someone tells a traveller to wait before quitting the Netherlands by French train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang on' is a pause, not gripping, and 'Holland' stands for the whole Netherlands by its international code.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon-lit is a sleeping car on a continental European train, the French term for such a coach.

clue.text: A latitude supported by tenor over another singer

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is supported sits on top, so the following pieces come underneath

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for latitude
T is the abbreviation for tenor
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A singer's range is backed up by a tenor alongside another vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' looks like the singer of the definition; it only gives T. 'Another' nods to that tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto sings the low female or high male voice part, so is one more kind of vocalist.

clue.text: Attitude when occupying height: scaffolder ready to go off at any moment

definitions.text: ready to go off at any moment

indicators.note: to occupy a space is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: HT is the abbreviation for height
an air is a manner or attitude
a rigger erects scaffolding

explanation.surface: A scaffolder high up has a jumpy attitude, liable to snap at any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attitude' is a manner or bearing, not a stance on an issue; a rigger is the worker who puts up scaffolding.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun with a hair-trigger fires at the slightest touch, so a hair-trigger temper can explode instantly.

clue.text: Former Queen upset business, sacking leader in interim period

indicators.note: in a down clue, to upset is to tip over, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth II

indicators.note: to sack the leader is to fire the one at the front, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: A former queen is overturned while a business fires its head in a stopgap period.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, the royal cipher of Elizabeth II, reverses to RE; AGENCY loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A regency is the stretch when a regent governs because the monarch is a child, absent or incapable.

clue.text: Island creature, flightless bird, caught between both sides

indicators.note: caught between two things is held inside them, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: left and right, L and R
the emu is a large Australian bird that cannot fly

explanation.surface: On an island, an animal and a flightless bird are trapped between two sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both sides' are left and right, L and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates found in the wild only on Madagascar and nearby islands, hence an island animal.

clue.text: Unimportant Nationalist in government for only a brief time?

definitions.note: adjectival, as in a lightning visit

parts.note: light as in trivial, of little weight
N is the abbreviation for Nationalist
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A minor nationalist joins government for just a short spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but is used as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightning visit or strike happens very quickly and lasts only a moment, like a flash in a storm.

clue.text: Government-appointed businessman sadly wrong about America, investing in US money

indicators.note: to invest something in a place is to put it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a cent is a US coin

indicators.note: things that go sadly end up in a sorry mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for the jumble
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A government-appointed businessman is sadly wrong about America while investing in dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' here places America inside the jumbled word rather than meaning 'concerning'; the whole result then splits the US coin after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown agent acts commercially on behalf of the British state, handling procurement and trade for it.

clue.text: Record of performance in unusual location regarding essential study?

indicators.note: what is in something sits inside it, so one piece goes within another
something unusual is out of the ordinary arrangement, so letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the jumble
a log records how a ship or flight performed

explanation.surface: A performance record ends up somewhere odd concerning a key study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essential' points at essence: the study is of being itself, which is why the definition is fair though cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontology is the philosophical inquiry into the nature of being and essence, so its adjective covers that study.

clue.text: Surprise publicity event not carrying through

indicators.note: failing to carry something through means stopping short, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: a publicity stunt is an event staged for attention

explanation.surface: A surprise publicity event falls flat and is not followed through.
explanation.walkthrough: STUNT stops one letter short.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to astonish them, a strong form of taking them by surprise.

clue.text: See company attending house surrounded by barrier, promising no drunken antics?

parts.note: a wall is a barrier
CO is the abbreviation for company
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A firm sees a walled house where no drunken rowdiness is promised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the old exclamation lo, as in 'lo and behold', and 'attending' just means placed beside.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink with little ethanol in it should not get anyone inebriated, so it guards against rowdy intoxicated behaviour.

clue.text: Turned on, tense and worried? Write music

indicators.note: something turned is facing the other way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
something eating at you worries you

explanation.surface: Excited, tense and anxious, a composer is urged to get writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned on' reads as excited, but 'Turned' acts on ON only. 'Ate' as worried is the 'what's eating you?' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to set something down in a system of written symbols, as composers do with a score.

clue.text: Youth? Fresh years, including golden one

Roman numeral for one
surface padding that supports the picture of youth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Years' wants to be the anagram fodder; it is part of the surface, and MINTY holds OR and I. Or is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: Minority is the legal state of being under the age of majority, a period of youth before adulthood.

clue.text: Sweetheart or duck, in crossword terms?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of a pair of doting lovers
second meaning: duck is both a zero score in cricket and a bird, so it splits into nil and fowl

explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of nothing, and love is nil in tennis; a duck is also a bird. Solvers use both readings, hence 'in crossword terms'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovebirds are small affectionate parrots, and the word means a besotted partner in a romantic couple.

clue.text: Entertainment penning lines linked to low aspect of heavenly body

L for line, doubled
to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the cattle sound, not a position, and the two lines are kept together inside the entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon shows different phases as it orbits, and the fully lit disc is one of those appearances.

clue.text: Complaint raised about Democratic Attorney-General's source of eats

parts.note: a beef is a grievance
D is the abbreviation for Democratic
initials of Attorney-General

explanation.definitionFit: A feedbag is the nosebag hung on a horse's head to hold its fodder, and informally any meal.

clue.text: Irregular Judge, old, accepting $1000

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: aged means old
G is a grand, a thousand dollars

explanation.walkthrough: G for a grand is US slang. G goes inside AGED, after J.
explanation.definitionFit: A jagged edge has uneven, sharp projections, so it is rough and irregular in outline.

clue.text: Guided up? Yes, getting day behind schedule

aye means yes
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.walkthrough: LED read upwards gives DEL, followed by AYE and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delayed is running late, held up past its scheduled time of arrival or completion.

clue.text: The whole attraction of Nice, say, in warmer period

parts.note: the sum is the whole amount

explanation.surface: The full charm of Nice is felt in the hot season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, and 'say' flags that the word is French: the sea is what draws visitors there.
explanation.definitionFit: Summer is the hottest of the four seasons, the warm stretch of the year between spring and autumn.

clue.text: Thus good is enshrined in lead character, though not at first

explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English as a formal word meaning consequently or so.

clue.text: Dressed up cellars, bringing in touch of hope — no longer this?

parts.note: taken as written for the jumble

parts.note: first letter of hope

clue.text: Part of some shimmering feature of lingerie?

explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is often made with a fine open net fabric, a common see-through detail on lacy underwear.

clue.text: Source of disease: cure a bit tricky, needing months

clue.text: Shout about a very intimidating presence

clue.text: Rising cheers surrounding Conservative legislation

clue.text: Told about particular backsliding, one being allowed to escape

parts.note: re means about or concerning
